working_title: County Down's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass, and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is arguably the most concentrated stretch of world-class links golf available to a UK visitor, yet most people only book Royal County Down and move on. This post makes the case for treating the whole County Down coastline as a circuit, covering the bucket-list flagship, the underrated scenic gem, and the low-key local links that rounds out a proper three-day trip.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (Newcastle, Co. Down) consistently ranked among the top 5 courses in the world; Golf Digest ranked it #1 on its World's 100 Greatest Courses list for 2024. Championship Links par 71; second course is the Annesley Links. Founded 1889; layout shaped by Old Tom Morris, Harry Vardon, and Harry Colt.
- RCD visitor access: designated visitor days only (reported as Mon, Tue, Thu mornings, Fri, Sun afternoons — confirm on booking); advance booking essential; visitor green fee reported at £450 for 2026 (source: thewanderinggolfers.com — treat as indicative, verify before publish as this is a third-party figure not from the club directly). No buggies; course has blind tee shots so a caddie is recommended. Visitor season broadly April–October.
- Ardglass Golf Club (Ardglass village, ~35 min drive from Newcastle): clifftop links on the County Down coast; noted for a spectacular opening hole carved into the cliff edge; clubhouse is reputedly housed in a 14th-century castle, described as one of the oldest buildings used as a golf clubhouse anywhere. Par 70. Ranked top 10 in Northern Ireland by Golf Digest (#6 in Ireland at time of ranking). Visitor-friendly and considerably more affordable than RCD — no specific green fee confirmed from an official source, so do not state a figure.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club (Cloughey, Ards Peninsula): par 69, 6,167 yards, designed by James Braid in 1902; described as the most easterly golf course in Ireland; traditional fast-and-firm links; Golfshake midweek guide fee from £35, weekend from £40 (from Golfshake listing — treat as indicative). Welcoming to visitors; relaxed atmosphere; accessible from Belfast.
- Royal Belfast Golf Club (Holywood, Co. Down): Ireland's oldest golf club (founded 1881); parkland course overlooking Belfast Lough; Harry Colt design; par 70. Good add-on for those combining golf with a Belfast stay.
- Practical logistics: Belfast (George Best City Airport or Belfast International) is the natural entry point. Newcastle (RCD) is roughly 50 min south of Belfast. Ardglass is a further 20–25 min along the coast. Kirkistown is on the Ards Peninsula, roughly an hour from Newcastle. A logical three-day routing: Day 1 RCD, Day 2 Ardglass, Day 3 Kirkistown or Royal Belfast.
- County Down's golfing tradition stretches to the 1880s; Royal Belfast (1881) is Ireland's oldest club.
- Mourne Mountains provide backdrop to RCD — a distinctive visual context worth mentioning.
- No Open Championship history at RCD to date, though it has hosted the Irish Open (2015 return after 76-year gap) and the 2024 Amgen Irish Open.
